note: French says si tu veux ('if you want'); English adds 'me to'.
proposed_target: Je peux marcher plus rapidement si tu veux.
proposed_english: I can walk faster if you want.

note: m'énerve means annoys/irritates me; 'makes me angry' is stronger and less exact.
proposed_target: Je ne peux te dire combien cela m'énerve.
proposed_english: I can't tell you how much that annoys me.

note: French says votre gentillesse without the English quantifier 'all'.
proposed_target: Je ne peux pas vous remercier suffisamment pour votre gentillesse.
proposed_english: I can't thank you enough for your kindness.

note: Je ne comprends pas means 'I don't understand', not inability 'I can't understand'.
proposed_target: Je ne comprends pas ce qu'il essaie de dire.
proposed_english: I don't understand what he is trying to say.

note: le refers to 'it'; English incorrectly says 'that'.
proposed_target: Je l'ai fait comme tu me l'as demandé.
proposed_english: I did it the way you asked me to.

note: English 'that which' is unnecessarily unnatural; French straightforwardly means 'what she asked me to do'.
proposed_target: J'ai fait ce qu'elle m'a demandé de faire.
proposed_english: I did what she asked me to do.

note: m'avaient dit is pluperfect; preserve the earlier past event.
proposed_target: Je n'ai pas fait ce qu'ils m'avaient dit de faire.
proposed_english: I didn't do what they had told me to do.

note: s'y prendre means 'go about it/how to proceed', which English 'do that' loses.
proposed_target: Je ne sais pas comment je vais m'y prendre.
proposed_english: I don't know how I'm going to go about it.

note: le refaire means 'do it again', not 'do that again'.
proposed_target: Je ne sais pas si je peux le refaire.
proposed_english: I don't know if I can do it again.

note: encore faire ceci most directly means 'still do this'; 'anymore' shifts the polarity nuance.
proposed_target: Je ne sais pas si je peux encore faire ceci.
proposed_english: I don't know if I can still do this.
